standard_prerequisites.name: Good quotient covers of differential graded modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies, at each induction step, the surjection P_i to M_i whose kernel continues the resolution and whose two-term structure produces the graded pieces.

standard_prerequisites.name: Admissibility of inclusions between sums of shifts and the resolution spectral sequence
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemma lemma-target-graded-projective; Homology, Lemma homology-lemma-good-resolution-gives-qis
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows the filtration inclusions are admissible monomorphisms, and turns the constructed resolution into the quasi-isomorphism P to M.

core_obligations: The inductive resolution (proof lines 2528-2539): starting from M_0 = M choose short exact sequences 0 to M_{i+1} to P_i to M_i to 0 with the maps from lemma-good-quotient, producing the resolution chain ending at M.

The total module (proof lines 2540-2555): set P to be the direct sum of the P_i with the grading P^n = direct sum over a + b = n of P_{-a}^b and the total-complex differential d_P(x) = f_{-a}(x) + (-1)^a d(x); with these conventions P is a differential graded A-module.

The property (P) filtration (proof lines 2556-2563): each P_i has the two-step filtration from its construction; interleaving the P_j with the P'_{i+1} gives differential graded submodules F_{2i}P and F_{2i+1}P whose successive quotients are direct sums of shifts of A, and by lemma-target-graded-projective the inclusions are admissible monomorphisms.
The quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 2564-2566): the augmentation P to M induced by P_0 to M is a quasi-isomorphism by the standard resolution lemma of Homology.
proof_roadmap: Build the resolution chain by iterating the good-quotient surjections.
Assemble the total differential graded module with its explicit grading and differential.
Interleave the two-step filtrations of the stages to get the property (P) filtration with admissible inclusions.
Conclude the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism through the homology resolution lemma.
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs, for every differential graded A-module, a quasi-isomorphic replacement with property (P) (statement lines 2518-2528). The proof (lines 2530-2566) is a construction carried through in the span: the inductive resolution from the good-quotient surjections, the total complex assembly with explicit grading and signed differential, the interleaved filtration whose graded pieces are sums of shifts of A with admissible inclusions verified through the projectivity lemma, and the closing quasi-isomorphism from the homology resolution lemma. H2: the assembly of the property (P) filtration from the two-step pieces is the non-formal content; this lemma is the engine behind every property-(P) reduction in the chapter.
